Done! The issue was floating-point precision in JavaScript. When converting decimal prices to cents (e.g., `39.95 * 100`), the result would be `3995.0000000000005` instead of exactly `3995`. I fixed it by wrapping the multiplication with `Math.round()` in three places:

1. `parseEuros()` in `src/money.js` — fixes prices from CLI arguments
2. `cellCents()` in `src/money.js` — fixes prices from CSV imports  
3. `decimalCommaToCents()` in `src/locale.js` — fixes European format prices (e.g., "12,99")

All prices now work, including Netflix (12.99), Spotify (10.99), and Gym (39.95).
